summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indologist and historian who earned an MPhil from Vikram University, where he was attested as a research scholar in 2014.
Mohammad Habib was an Indian historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Aligarh Muslim University (around 1912–1916), and New College, Oxford (around 1916–1919).

Mohan G. Dhadphale is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

Mokurai Shimaji was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as Geschäftsführer at Nishi Hongan-ji (1870), founded Chiyoda Jogakuen (1888), and was the 25th head priest of Gankyo-ji (1892–1905).

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was a research fellow at Humboldt University and taught at Heidelberg University.

Monica Esposito was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. She completed a PhD at Paris Diderot University and University of Paris, and became an Associate Professor at Kyoto University in 2003 after postdoctoral fellowships in Venice, Paris, and Kansai.

Monica L. Smith is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan (ca. 1991–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2002 as a professor.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (1844–1858) and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887, founding the Indian Institute.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach is an Indologist and linguist. She earned her doctorate under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow at the Free University of Berlin, taught at the University of Bonn and University of Bamberg, and served as professor of modern Indology at Heidelberg (1990–2006).
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who has held posts at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2010 and 2026.

Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich, where she became a professor (~2001–2016), and later led research projects at the Saxon Academy and Leipzig University.
Moodeen Sheriff was an Indian medical practitioner and Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under K. R. Norman, served as professor at Sendai National College of Technology (~1986–2004), and was president of Hosen Gakuen College (~2004–2014).

Moritz Abraham Stern was a mathematician and linguist who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen, completing his doctorate under Carl Friedrich Gauss. He was appointed Extraordinarius at Göttingen (1829–1884), succeeding Gauss in 1858.

Moriz Haupt was a German classical philologist and linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Leipzig (1841–1851) and later held the chair of Roman literature at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and with Georg Bühler. He worked with Max Müller at Oxford, taught at Visva-Bharati University, and served as professor at the German University Prague (~1902–1934).

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He has held teaching posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, and the University of Iowa, where he is an associate professor.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist who studied at University College London. He directed the National Museum of Wales, the London Museum (1926–1944), and served as Director-General of Archæology in India (1944–1948) and Honorary Secretary of the British Academy (~1949–1968).

Morton Klass was an anthropologist who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, completing his doctorate in 1959. He held faculty posts at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).
